sn47.6:1.1: “Bhikkhus, once in the past a hawk suddenly swooped down and seized a quail.
sn47.6:1.2: Then, while the quail was being carried off by the hawk, he lamented:
sn47.6:1.3: ‘We were so unlucky, of so little merit! We strayed out of our own resort into the domain of others.
sn47.6:1.4: If we had stayed in our own resort today, in our own ancestral domain, this hawk wouldn’t have stood a chance against me in a fight.’—
sn47.6:1.5: ‘But what is your own resort, quail, what is your own ancestral domain?’—
sn47.6:1.6: ‘The freshly ploughed field covered with clods of soil.’
sn47.6:1.7: “Then the hawk, confident of her own strength, not boasting of her own strength, released the quail, saying:
sn47.6:1.8: ‘Go now, quail, but even there you won’t escape me.’
sn47.6:2.1: “Then, bhikkhus, the quail went to a freshly ploughed field covered with clods of soil. Having climbed up on a large clod, he stood there and addressed the hawk:
sn47.6:2.2: ‘Come get me now, hawk! Come get me now, hawk!’
sn47.6:2.3: “Then the hawk, confident of her own strength, not boasting of her own strength, folded up both her wings and suddenly swooped down on the quail.
sn47.6:2.4: But when the quail knew, ‘That hawk has come close,’ he slipped inside that clod,
sn47.6:2.5: and the hawk shattered her breast right on the spot.
sn47.6:2.6: So it is, bhikkhus, when one strays outside one’s own resort into the domain of others.
sn47.6:3.1: “Therefore, bhikkhus, do not stray outside your own resort into the domain of others.
sn47.6:3.2: Mara will gain access to those who stray outside their own resort into the domain of others; Mara will get a hold on them.
sn47.6:3.3: “And what is not a bhikkhu’s own resort but the domain of others?
sn47.6:3.4: It is the five cords of sensual pleasure.
sn47.6:3.6: Forms cognizable by the eye that are desirable, lovely, agreeable, pleasing, sensually enticing, tantalizing.
sn47.6:3.10: Tactile objects cognizable by the body that are desirable, lovely, agreeable, pleasing, sensually enticing, tantalizing. These are the five cords of sensual pleasure.
sn47.6:3.11: This is what is not a bhikkhu’s own resort but the domain of others.
sn47.6:4.1: “Move in your own resort, bhikkhus, in your own ancestral domain.
sn47.6:4.2: Mara will not gain access to those who move in their own resort, in their own ancestral domain; Mara will not get a hold on them.
sn47.6:4.3: “And what is a bhikkhu’s resort, his own ancestral domain?
sn47.6:4.5: It is the four establishments of mindfulness.
sn47.6:4.7: Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu dwells contemplating the body in the body, ardent, clearly comprehending, mindful, having removed covetousness and displeasure in regard to the world.
sn47.6:4.8: He dwells contemplating feelings in feelings …
sn47.6:4.10: phenomena in phenomena, ardent, clearly comprehending, mindful, having removed covetousness and displeasure in regard to the world.
sn47.6:4.11: This is a bhikkhu’s resort, his own ancestral domain.”
